## Reuse the boundary

The page source embeds any registered same-origin route with one directive:

```{.markdown shortcodes=false}
{{< bonito route="/widgets/control-panel" title="Cable controls" height="34rem" >}}
```

Widget implementations live in `src/widgets.jl`. Keep domain-specific controls in their own Julia files, return a Bonito `App`, and register only their route in the publisher.

For reusable toolbars, bind stable action names to the module that owns their meaning:

```julia
module PlotTools
function handle_toolbar(state, event)
    state[] = "$(event.namespace).$(event.action)"
end
end

binding = ToolbarBinding(PlotTools, session_state; namespace=:impedance_plot)

tools = toolbar(
    [
        ToolbarButton(:reset_view; icon=:reset, tooltip="Reset view"),
        ToolbarButton(:fit_view; icon=:fit, label="Fit view"),
        ToolbarDropdown(
            :display_layer,
            [:nominal => "Nominal", :envelope => "Envelope"];
            icon=:layers,
            label="Layer"
        ),
    ];
    binding,
    orientation=:horizontal,
    size=:medium
)
```

The callback receives a `ToolbarEvent(namespace, action, value)`. Names use lowercase `snake_case`; the constructor rejects duplicate actions and invalid identifiers before the page is served.

Repeaters keep collection mechanics separate from a row's locally meaningful fields and controls:

```julia
function cable_entry(values=(name="Cable 01", enabled=true, model="Solid"))
    name = TextField(values.name)
    enabled = Checkbox(values.enabled)
    model = Dropdown(["Solid", "Stranded"]; index=values.model == "Solid" ? 1 : 2)

    fields = (name=name.value, enabled=enabled.value, model=model.value)
    content = DOM.div(name, enabled, model; class="my-cable-row")
    return RepeatEntry(fields, content)
end

cables = Repeater(
    cable_entry;
    initial=2,
    duplicate=cable_entry,
    min_entries=1,
    max_entries=12,
    label="Cable definitions"
)

values = snapshot(cables)
```

Power-system canvases accept a versioned diagram and expose only a validated
topology snapshot to Julia. The editor remains an authoring surface, not an
execution engine:

```julia
canvas = PowerSystemCanvas(diagram)
topology = snapshot(canvas) # nothing until the browser publishes its first snapshot
```

File upload destinations are supplied by the workbench. Browser filenames remain metadata and never determine server paths:

```julia
target = UploadTarget(
    DirectoryUploadStore(joinpath(state.workspace, "inputs")),
    "network-model";
    extensions=[".json", ".csv"],
    max_bytes=20 * 1024 * 1024,
    retention=:persistent
)

input_file = UploadField(
    target;
    label="Network model",
    hint="Validated workbench input"
)

input_file.value   # Observable{Union{Nothing, UploadedFile}}
input_file.status  # :empty → :uploading → :validating → :ready
```

Geographic maps compose that upload slot with a persistent browser renderer. The tag vocabulary belongs to the workbench using the component:

```julia
upload = UploadField(kml_target)
route_map = GeographicMap(
    KMLUploadSource(upload);
    tags=[
        "terminal" => "Terminal",
        "joint" => "Cable joint",
        "survey" => "Survey reference",
    ]
)

route_map.references[]
```

`fields` may contain any number of observables nested in named tuples, tuples, arrays, or dictionaries. `content` may contain input fields, checkboxes, dropdowns, figures, prose, or any other Bonito-renderable composition. Supply `extract=fields -> ...` to `RepeatEntry` when a row needs a specialized snapshot.
